references.question: How should multiple aggregate versions be handled?
references.title: Causal Inference Under Multiple Versions of Treatment
references.finding: An aggregate value may conceal versions with different potential outcomes; versions or their assignment distribution must be specified.
references.limitations: Method does not establish case-specific causality.

references.question: Can constructed measures support causal interpretation?
references.title: Constructed Measures and Causal Inference
references.finding: Composite measures can sometimes receive a causal interpretation through explicit underlying versions, but unknown versions impede intervention and identification.
references.limitations: Does not validate any PSYWERX composite.

references.question: Can macro variables be causal?
references.title: Multi-Level Cause-Effect Systems
references.finding: Macro causal variables can be coherent when linked to experimental micro-level interventions and stable causal partitions.
references.limitations: The formal result does not establish empirical evidence for repository routes.

references.question: What is required for network interventions?
references.title: Causal Inference for Social Network Data
references.finding: Network causal estimands require explicit interventions on treatment or network structure and handling of interference; a scalar metric alone is not the intervention.
references.limitations: No PSYWERX route is identified by this methods paper.

references.question: Does circadian phase affect sleep propensity independently of time awake?
references.title: Paradoxical timing of the circadian rhythm of sleep propensity serves to consolidate sleep and wakefulness in humans
references.finding: Forced desynchrony separates circadian and homeostatic processes and supports a circadian contribution to sleep consolidation.
references.limitations: Eight men; sleep propensity/consolidation is not identical to broad sleep duration.

references.question: Does homeostatic pressure modify the circadian effect?
references.title: Sleep restriction masks the influence of the circadian process on sleep propensity
references.finding: Circadian modulation was pronounced under a normal sleep-wake ratio and masked under severe restriction, demonstrating version and interaction dependence.
references.limitations: Male laboratory sample; does not identify the repository's broad aggregate contrast.

references.question: Is scalar cultural distance causally interpretable?
references.title: Toward a more in-depth measurement of cultural distance
references.finding: Distance magnitude alone omits dimension, direction, symmetry and context, producing ambiguous interpretations.
references.limitations: Country-level international-business construct, not adjacent-generation norm entrenchment directly.

references.question: Can staffing ratios identify causal effects?
references.title: How do hospitals respond to input regulation? Evidence from the California nurse staffing mandate
references.finding: A defined staffing mandate changed staffing time and multiple organizational margins, including capacity, showing that the intervention version matters beyond a scalar ratio.
references.limitations: Hospital nursing does not establish territorial administrative reach or generic service capacity.

references.question: Do ratio changes yield uniform outcomes?
references.title: The effect of a hospital nurse staffing mandate on patient health outcomes
references.finding: The mandate changed ratios but did not yield relative improvements in measured safety outcomes, cautioning against treating ratio movement as a uniform mechanism.
references.limitations: Outcome and institutional setting differ from the PSYWERX target.

references.question: Can topology affect adoption?
references.title: The spread of behavior in an online social network experiment
references.finding: Randomized network structures can change behavioral diffusion, supporting a topology-level causal question when the exact treatment and exposure are specified.
references.limitations: The manipulation is topology, not an isolated scalar local-clustering intervention.

references.question: Can a group-level goal condition affect cooperation or performance?
references.title: The effect of group-level performance goals on group performance
references.finding: Assigned group goals affected performance conditionally through coordination and action planning, supporting a bounded group-context question.
references.limitations: The manipulation is an assigned group goal, not the repository's measured goal-alignment aggregate or cooperation-prevalence endpoint.

caseReviews.question: Can circadian alignment independently affect sleep duration rather than only summarize phase and schedule?
caseReviews.causalContrast: A specified shift of sleep opportunity relative to measured circadian phase, holding the sleep-opportunity window and prior wake history explicit.
caseReviews.candidateMechanism: Circadian phase-dependent sleep propensity and consolidation interacting with homeostatic pressure.
caseReviews.sourceQualityAccessDepth: Controlled forced-desynchrony studies; abstracts reviewed; small male laboratory samples.
caseReviews.supportingFindings: Circadian phase has an effect separable from elapsed wake time on sleep propensity/consolidation.
caseReviews.nullOrContraryFindings: Severe sleep restriction masks circadian modulation, so effects are not invariant across versions.
caseReviews.limitations: The repository aggregate combines several alignment domains and the target is broad sleep duration; no exact executable contrast/profile exists.
caseReviews.remainingUncertainty: Which alignment component and intervention policy defines the source without overlap or double count.

caseReviews.question: Can scalar adjacent-generation cultural distance act as a causal source for norm entrenchment?
caseReviews.causalContrast: A direction- and dimension-specific change between adjacent generation profiles within one cultural community.
caseReviews.candidateMechanism: Intergenerational mismatch could alter transmission, contestation, or reinforcement of a focal norm.
caseReviews.supportingFindings: Cultural-distance measurement requires dimension, direction, symmetry, and context.
caseReviews.nullOrContraryFindings: Equal scalar distance does not imply equal profile change or mechanism.
caseReviews.limitations: No exact derivation or aggregate-level causal identification for the repository route.
caseReviews.remainingUncertainty: Whether a dimension-specific contrast can be defined without embedding the target norm.

caseReviews.question: Can caseload pressure independently affect service-delivery capacity?
caseReviews.causalContrast: A specified demand change, staffing/time change, or policy that alters caseload pressure while separately defining service capacity.
caseReviews.candidateMechanism: Workload pressure may reduce attention, throughput, quality, or implementation reliability.
caseReviews.sourceQualityAccessDepth: Quasi-experimental staffing-policy study at full-text depth; canonical repository sources inspected.
caseReviews.supportingFindings: Defined staffing regulation changes multiple operational margins and demonstrates that input interventions can affect capacity.
caseReviews.nullOrContraryFindings: The source and target both use staffing/capacity content, creating circular overlap in the current definitions.
caseReviews.limitations: Evidence does not identify the exact caseload-pressure aggregate independently of its constituents.
caseReviews.remainingUncertainty: Whether a noncontaminated target and explicit intervention version can be specified.

caseReviews.question: Can staffing adequacy independently enable territorial administrative reach?
caseReviews.causalContrast: A specified staffing intervention, workload intervention, or skill-composition policy producing a bound adequacy change.
caseReviews.candidateMechanism: Qualified deployable labor can extend the institution's consistent geographic administration.
caseReviews.sourceQualityAccessDepth: Quasi-experimental policy studies at full-text and abstract depth.
caseReviews.supportingFindings: Mandates can move staffing ratios and organizational responses.
caseReviews.nullOrContraryFindings: Ratio changes did not produce uniform downstream outcome improvements.
caseReviews.limitations: Hospital staffing is not territorial administration; equal ratios can reflect different staff, workload, and skill versions.
caseReviews.remainingUncertainty: The intervention policy, reference workload, skill mix, and mechanism needed for an invariant contrast.

caseReviews.question: Can local clustering function as a contextual source for social reinforcement multiplicity?
caseReviews.causalContrast: An exact topology transformation on a bound graph that changes neighborhood closure while retaining state, boundary, window, and exposure semantics.
caseReviews.candidateMechanism: Closed neighborhoods can create redundant independent reinforcement exposures.
caseReviews.sourceQualityAccessDepth: Randomized network experiment and network-causal methods literature.
caseReviews.supportingFindings: Randomly assigned network topology can alter diffusion behavior.
caseReviews.nullOrContraryFindings: The experiment does not isolate a scalar local-clustering intervention or the exact reinforcement-multiplicity endpoint.
caseReviews.limitations: Identical clustering values can hide different topologies and actor exposures.
caseReviews.remainingUncertainty: Exact state transition, exposure mapping, contribution identity, and route-specific evidence.

caseReviews.question: Can goal alignment function as a contextual group source for cooperation prevalence?
caseReviews.causalContrast: A specified collective-episode intervention that aligns member goals without defining cooperation as part of alignment.
caseReviews.candidateMechanism: Shared goal direction can support coordination and reduce effort conflict.
caseReviews.sourceQualityAccessDepth: Group-level experiment at abstract depth plus canonical repository evidence.
caseReviews.supportingFindings: Assigned group goals can affect group performance through coordination/action planning.
caseReviews.nullOrContraryFindings: Effects are conditional; assigned goals are not the same construct as measured goal alignment.
caseReviews.limitations: The exact alignment aggregate, contribution overlap, and cooperation-prevalence endpoint are not identified.
caseReviews.remainingUncertainty: Whether an episode-specific contrast and independent contribution can be supported.
